resumen: The spies promised to deal kindly and truly with Rahab, and she let them down by a cord through the window of her house on the wall. A letter about a word that is kept.

versos.texto: The men said to her, “Our life for yours, if you don’t talk about this business of ours; and it shall be, when the LORD gives us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with you.”
Then she let them down by a cord through the window; for her house was on the side of the wall, and she lived on the wall.

reflexion: The spies answer Rahab's request. They give her their word, and they stake their own lives on it. They set one condition: that she not talk about this business of theirs. And they make her a promise: when the Lord gives them the land, they will deal kindly and truly with her.

Kindness and truth. A kindness that doesn't stay in words, and words that are kept. Then Rahab acts. She lets them down by a cord through the window. Her house was on the side of the city wall. She lived on the wall.

All of this happens in a time of war. Helping those men was a serious risk for her. Rahab didn't have everything worked out. She had a promise, and with it she took the next step. Maybe today you can't see the end of the road either. Only the step in front of you.
God is faithful to his word. And he invites us to treat others with kindness and truth. Today you can keep a small promise, or tell a truth with kindness.
dedicatoria: This letter is for you, who take a step without seeing the whole road. You don't walk alone.
oracion: Lord, thank you that your word is faithful and your mercy never fails. Teach us to live with kindness and truth, and to trust you at every step. In Jesus' name, amen.
